problem: LLM-based zero-shot ObjectNav pipelines rely on a fragile cascade of mapping, segmentation, text translation and planning. Text cannot express geometry or spatial layout, and depth/localization errors corrupt the map. VLMs cannot directly output navigable 3D waypoints.
motivation: A mapless approach that works from raw RGB/RGB-D with a VLM would cut latency and compounding errors. VLMs are better at multiple-choice image selection than at 3D geometric reasoning. Showing imagined future views at sensible waypoints lets the VLM reason about distant or unclear regions.
key_idea: Predict human-like future waypoints with a learned Where2Imagine module, render the views there with a novel-view-synthesis model, and have a VLM pick the best imagined image, which a PointNav policy then executes.
insight: Imagined future views make the candidates semantically distinct, which helps the VLM. In the HM3D ablation with real images, SR rises from 43.0 without imagination to 55.0 with uniform 2 m imagination, and to 64.0 with Where2Imagine. NVS quality is the bottleneck: with NVS the SR is 56.0, versus 64.0 with real views, and ImagineNav-Oracle (real images) reaches 62.0 on HM3D. The waypoint distance T matters, and the small ResNet-18 trained from scratch beats larger pretrained backbones.
method: Where2Imagine: ResNet-18 trained from scratch on Habitat-Web human ObjectNav demonstrations (MP3D). It maps the current RGB to the relative pose (dx, dy, theta) of the pose T=11 frames later. Low-depth (<0.3) images are filtered out and angular deviation is limited to ±30°.

Novel view synthesis: a pretrained long-term photometrically consistent diffusion NVS model (Yu et al. 2023), not fine-tuned. It generates the view at the predicted relative pose for each of 6 headings spaced 60° apart.

VLM high-level planner: GPT-4o-mini receives the 6 stitched, labeled imagined images plus the goal. A prompt prioritizes target discovery, then unexplored potential, and returns JSON {Reason, Choice}.
PointNav controller: a VER-trained PointNav policy drives the agent to the chosen waypoint. Each new arrival triggers a new imagine-select cycle until the target is found.
Mapless loop: no map, no detector, and no history; only the current panorama is used at each iteration, which causes local traps.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o-mini (frozen) as planner; ResNet-18 (trained from scratch) for Where2Imagine; pretrained diffusion NVS (frozen); VER PointNav policy (RL-trained)
setting.model_size: ResNet-18 11.4M params for Where2Imagine; GPT-4o-mini size unspecified
setting.training_data: Where2Imagine trained on Habitat-Web human demonstrations (80k ObjectNav + 12k Pick&Place; MP3D trajectories used). VLM and NVS are used zero-shot with no ObjectNav fine-tuning.
setting.observation: egocentric panoramic RGB-D (6 views, 60° apart) on-board; no map
setting.action_space: Discrete low-level actions (Stop, MoveAhead 0.25 m, TurnLeft/Right 30°, LookUp, LookDown), via PointNav sub-goals selected from imagined waypoints
setting.privileged: none for the main method; the ImagineNav-Oracle variant uses real images at candidate poses

results: On HM3D, ImagineNav (mapless, zero-shot VLM) reaches 53.0 SR / 23.8 SPL, slightly above the map-based VLFM (52.5 SR, though VLFM has higher SPL of 30.4), and beats PixNav (37.9) and ESC (39.2). On HSSD it gets 51.0 SR / 24.9 SPL, above VoroNav (41.0 / 23.2). With real images (Oracle) SR rises to 62.0 (HM3D) and 59.0 (HSSD).
limitations: Performance is limited by the quality of the off-the-shelf NVS model, which can hallucinate objects or misalign with reality (NVS 56 vs. real 64 SR).
No history or memory, so the agent gets trapped in local optima in long-horizon navigation.
Evaluation covers only 100-200 episodes in simulation, with no real-robot tests; the false-failure issue of the simulator also affects results.
builds_on: Long-term photometrically consistent NVS (Yu et al. 2023)
